bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital efficiency framed as the core narrative: ROCE (annualised for Q1FY27) rising 7.5% / 11.3% / 21.2% / 26.8% across FY24 / FY25 / FY26 / Q1FY27.
- Capital employed (defined as Net Worth + Net Debt) of Rs 1,658 / 1,791 / 2,073 / 2,211 Cr over Q1FY24-Q1FY27, i.e. scale compounding on a broadly flat capital base.
- Working capital days improved 42 / 34 / 28 / 29 (FY24 / FY25 / FY26 / Q1FY27) and fixed asset turnover rose 9.1 / 9.1 / 9.9 / 10.7x, attributed to "Rising salience of asset light business such as Fashion and House of Nykaa".
- No dividend, buyback, debt quantum or fund-raising policy is disclosed in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Largest specialty beauty retail store network in India - 313 beauty stores across 99 cities, with a record 76 new stores added in FY2026
- Preferred gateway for global beauty brands entering India - L'Oreal, Estee Lauder, Shiseido, Puig and Amorepacific partner with Nykaa, and 200+ international beauty brands were added in FY2026 including exclusive launches
- Assortment breadth and curation - 10,000+ global and domestic brands on the platform, 4,400+ beauty and personal care brands and ~5,700 fashion brands as on March 31, 2026
- Cumulative customer base of more than 55 million (45 million beauty, 11 million fashion), described as India's largest and most valuable beauty customer base
- Owned-brand building capability - House of Nykaa combines consumer insight, in-house R&D, packaging expertise and 360-degree marketing, with brands sold across Nykaa, stores, brand-owned channels, general trade, marketplaces and exports
- B2B reach into the unorganised beauty retail market - Superstore by Nykaa serves nearly 5,00,000 onboarded retailers across 1,200 cities
- Premium customer mix - Nykaa Fashion's Average Order Value of Rs 4,600 is around 60% higher than comparable platforms, and Nykaa customers spend roughly 5x the India average
- Fulfilment density supporting service levels - 70% of beauty orders across the top 110 cities are delivered within 24-36 hours
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Product quality and safety across a third-party supply base — The business model depends on third-party suppliers and partner manufacturers, so ingredients, formulations and finished products need rigorous oversight; any lapse could lead to regulatory scrutiny and weaken customer confidence in products offered on the platform. Mitigated through responsible supplier selection, manufacturing aligned with Good Manufacturing Practices, consumer testing and post-development validation.
- Data privacy and cybersecurity — As an e-commerce platform handling sensitive customer data, any unauthorised access, misuse or fraud could lead to financial implications, regulatory scrutiny and a decline in customer confidence. This is the only material issue the BRSR classifies as a pure Risk with negative financial implications only. Mitigated through advanced cybersecurity controls, periodic internal and external technology assessments, ISO 27001 certified processes and controls, monitoring of high-risk activity and review of seller transaction histories.
- Talent attraction and retention in a high-attrition market — Nykaa operates in a dynamic talent market characterised by high attrition and intense competition for skilled professionals. The BRSR reports permanent-employee turnover of 32% in FY2025-26 (30% in FY2024-25), with female turnover at 40%. Mitigated through learning and development, engagement initiatives, employer branding and induction of experienced professionals into critical leadership roles.
- Responsible supply chain exposed to geopolitical, climate and infrastructure shocks — The value chain remains sensitive to geopolitical developments, climate-related events, infrastructure limitations and rising sustainability expectations, each of which can influence operating performance, customer experience and brand perception. Mitigated through a decentralised, locally anchored supply chain, MSME engagement for packaging procurement and contractual human-rights expectations for suppliers and partners.
- Responsible marketing, service delivery and consumer-protection compliance — Customer-related risk can emerge from breakdowns in service delivery, non-compliant or inaccurate promotional messaging, and evolving legal obligations including ASCI norms and consumer protection requirements. Mitigated through an integrated multi-channel marketing approach that reduces dependence on any one medium, labelling compliance, and structured grievance and satisfaction tracking.
- Climate change, GHG emissions and energy-efficiency regulation — Climate-related disruptions including extreme weather events may affect operational continuity, while compliance with evolving emissions regulations could place additional pressure on operating costs. The Company says it is progressively incorporating renewable energy across facilities while enhancing operational and energy efficiency.
- Packaging and waste management under evolving regulation — Listed as a material risk-and-opportunity in the BRSR material-issues table in light of evolving regulation; the rationale text is cut off in the routed extract, so only the identification of the issue is supported.
- Activity and geographic concentration — Structural concentration disclosed rather than labelled as a risk: retail sale via e-commerce accounts for 95% of the listed entity's turnover, markets served are Pan India with International shown as Not Applicable (exports sit in a separate subsidiary, FSN International), and 100% of loans and advances and 100% of investments are with related parties. Customer grievances filed were 5,879 in FY2025-26 (6,933 in FY2024-25), all resolved with none pending.

business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: FSN E-Commerce Ventures (Nykaa) sells and distributes beauty, fashion and wellness products to Indian consumers through its own online platforms and apps and through an owned physical retail network, complemented by a B2B distribution arm and a portfolio of owned consumer brands. The platform curates global, homegrown and emerging brands and pairs them with content-led discovery, expert guidance and in-store experiences, serving tech-savvy consumers with a particular focus on Gen Z and millennials. Alongside the marketplace and inventory-led retail business, House of Nykaa builds and scales the company's own beauty and fashion brands, while Superstore by Nykaa supplies the unorganised beauty retail trade.

outlook.body: House of Nykaa brands scaling to 12+ brands; international expansion (Kay Beauty in UK/GCC); Nykaa Perfumery and experiential retail formats; AI-driven personalization unlocking higher LTV; Superstore as primary D2C distribution channel for emerging brands
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Deliver profitable growth with efficient capital utilisation and strong unit economics, with capital allocation anchored in Return on Capital Employed.
- Maintain balance-sheet and working-capital discipline - shorten the operating cycle through faster inventory turnover and continue reducing net debt.
- Run a content-first omnichannel ecosystem that integrates content, commerce and convenience so customers can discover, learn and shop across digital platforms and physical stores.
- Curate a differentiated assortment of global, homegrown and owned brands using consumer insights, market intelligence and trend forecasting, refreshed through innovative products, exclusive launches and emerging categories.
- Embed Generative AI and analytics across customer service and customer experience - AI-powered self-service, voice bots for order queries, personalised recommendations and virtual consultations.
- Deepen collaborative planning with brand partners through the CPFR framework and an integrated S&OP process with AI-powered demand sensing, supported by an Auto Replenishment System that manages lead times and demand variability.
- Automate and digitise operations - EDI-based partner integration, a digitised end-to-end order lifecycle, faster order processing, better fill rates and improved inventory freshness.
- Build sustainable and responsible partnerships - responsible sourcing, expanded use of recyclable and eco-friendly packaging, reduction of single-use plastics through supplier collaboration, localised fulfilment and MSME support.
- Rationalise the legal-entity structure to consolidate businesses and remove duplication - the online B2B beauty business was demerged from FSN Distribution into Nykaa E-Retail and Iluminar Media was amalgamated into Nykaa Fashion, both operationalised with effect from May 29, 2025.
- Increase ownership of owned-brand subsidiaries - stake in Dot & Key Wellness raised to 90.06%, Earth Rhythm to ~75.83%, and the remaining 40% of Nudge Wellness acquired to make it a wholly-owned subsidiary.
- Improve financial transparency for shareholders through granular segment-level disclosure for Beauty and Fashion and sustained investor engagement (quarterly earnings calls, quarterly revenue updates, an annual Investor Day, store and Nykaaland visits).
- The Company has formulated a Dividend Distribution Policy under Regulation 43A of the Listing Regulations setting out the internal and external factors the Board considers in determining pay-out. For FY2025-26 the Board did not recommend any dividend on equity shares and decided to retain the entire profit for the year in the statement of profit and loss, i.e. the stance remains full reinvestment. Management describes its capital allocation strategy as "firmly anchored in Return on Capital Employed", combining balance-sheet discipline (working capital efficiency and net debt reduction) with a commitment to generate higher operating cash flow through efficient working capital management and optimised capital expenditure. Forward intent is to keep investing in the core growth engines while taking a phased approach to new, emerging opportunity areas through either organic initiatives or strategic inorganic acquisitions. The Company reports a long-term credit rating of CRISIL A - Stable. As on March 31, 2026 the Company has no associate or joint venture; it has eleven direct subsidiaries and ten step-down subsidiaries.
- BRSR disclosures carry Reasonable Assurance in line with ISAE 3000 (Revised) from TUV India Pvt. Ltd., covering FSN E-Commerce Ventures Limited and its subsidiary Nykaa E-Retail Limited.
- 100% of R&D investment in both FY2025-26 and FY2024-25 was directed at improving own-brand product formulations by incorporating non-hazardous and environmentally friendly ingredients.
- 0.29% of capital expenditure in FY2025-26 (0.24% in FY2024-25) was spent on upgrading infrastructure at offices and warehouses with energy-efficient technologies to reduce electricity consumption and lower carbon emissions.
- The Company has formally adopted a Sustainable Sourcing Policy and states it has procedures in place for sustainable sourcing.
- Progressive incorporation of renewable energy across facilities alongside continuing improvement in operational and energy efficiency (stated as the mitigation for the climate-change material issue; no dated target or renewable-share percentage is disclosed).
- Packaging and waste commitments with value-chain partners: expand the use of recyclable and eco-friendly packaging, reduce single-use plastics through supplier collaboration, and enable localised fulfilment to lower environmental impact.
- Supplier inclusion: 8,700+ MSME partners, with MSMEs engaged for packaging procurement and supported in building a resilient supply ecosystem.
- Human rights expectations are reinforced across suppliers and partners through contractual provisions; awareness programmes for selected value chain partners cover fire safety, emergency response, road safety and POSH guidelines.
- Governance and ethics: an Anti-Corruption and Anti-Bribery Policy applying to Directors, Officers, Employees, subsidiaries, affiliates, contractors and suppliers; annual Code of Conduct and POSH training; a whistle-blower Speak-up helpline run by an external agency with direct access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee. Nil fines/penalties and no bribery/corruption disciplinary actions in FY2025-26.
- Information security: the Company's processes and controls are ISO 27001 certified, supported by periodic internal and external technology assessments.
- Diversity: women are 27.27% of the Board of Directors (3 of 11) and 40% of Key Management Personnel (2 of 5); women are 48.20% of total employees.
- Customer grievance performance: 100% of customer complaints resolved in FY2026, with no complaints pending resolution at year-end across any stakeholder group.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Nykaa's expansion in FY2026 was footprint- and network-led rather than plant-led. The beauty retail network was expanded by a record 76 new stores during the year, and the premium format was scaled with 15 new Nykaa Luxe stores plus dedicated Perfumery stores for luxury fragrances; Nykaa Now was rolled out to enable rapid delivery. On fulfilment, the CFO's message describes a network of 44 warehouses across 15 cities that "significantly strengthened our delivery capabilities and customer experience", with the result that 70% of beauty orders across the top 110 cities are now delivered within 24-36 hours. Assortment expansion accompanied the physical build-out: 200+ new international beauty brands were launched in FY2026, and Nykaa Fashion added 1,250+ brands during the year (680+ in women's fashion, 280+ in home and accessories, 170+ in men's fashion and 120+ in kids' wear). The CFO states that capital expenditure during FY2026 "was deployed exclusively towards high-velocity physical store expansion (76 additions) and strengthening our technology infrastructure". Within total capex, the BRSR reports that 0.29% in FY2025-26 (0.24% in FY2024-25) went to upgrading infrastructure at offices and warehouses with energy-efficient technologies. Looking forward, management says it will continue to expand the physical retail store footprint, make deliberate investments to acquire new customers and improve order-to-delivery speeds, leverage technology and automation for efficiency, optimise capital expenditure, and take a phased approach to investing in new, emerging opportunity areas through either organic initiatives or strategic inorganic acquisitions. No commissioning timelines, project names or rupee project budgets are disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Asset productivity is being lifted by lower warehouse and store intensity relative to turnover and by the rising salience of asset-light businesses such as Fashion and House of Nykaa.
- Management attributes margin expansion to operating leverage - "operational excellence coupled with scale efficiencies".
- Working capital efficiency improved sharply, with the operating cycle reducing to 28 days from 34 days in FY2025 aided by faster inventory turnover; inventory days were lower by 4 days while receivables improved by 2 days.
- The return profile is being driven by balance-sheet discipline, with net debt nearly halving during the year.
- Demand engagement metrics are the stated growth drivers - monthly average unique visitors, annual unique transacting customers and orders all grew, supported by content-led discovery and a curated assortment.
- Trust, authenticity, quality assurance and personalised, expert-assisted experiences are cited as the basis for repeat engagement and customer loyalty.

deepdive.thesis: Nykaa delivered record revenue and profitability growth in FY26, with EBITDA margin expanding to 7.5% and PAT margin hitting 2%, driven by accelerated growth in House of Nykaa brands and profitable turnaround in Fashion; the company is now a dominant omnichannel platform in beauty and fashion with AI-enhanced customer acquisition and brand partnerships like Nike and H&M creating new revenue streams.

open.item: Depreciating rupee, high oil prices and inflation could pressure consumption and prompt brand price hikes (not yet passed on); direct imports are a small, fully-hedged (2-3 months) portion, and beauty is a resilient 'small luxury'.

April/May FY27 growth momentum has been good and management broadly expects to sustain the recent mid-20s growth zone, while staying cautious on macro (currency/oil/inflation) and expecting AI-led benefits on both top line and costs.

Nykaa Now (30 min-2 hr) network built out to ~75-80 rapid stores across top 7 metros covering 80-90% of relevant pincodes; FY27 plan is to market it aggressively so it contributes a much more meaningful percent of orders.
Management sees the possibility of double-digit EBITDA margin over the next 3-4 years as growth businesses mature and marketing/S&D costs fall (hedged, not firm guidance).

Beauty retail on track to reach ~500 stores over 3-4 years (guidance given ~2 years ago); FY27 plan ~50-70 new doors (~170-180 more over next 2-3 years), densifying Tier 2/3 towns from a current base of 313 stores in 99 cities.

Nykaa now operates Kiehl's India business (boutiques + kiehls.com + exclusive Nykaa.com retail) and builds/operates Charlotte Tilbury's exclusive brand stores (first in APAC, exclusivity extended 6+ years), a full-stack model it hopes to replicate with more brands.
Committed to generating higher operating cash flows, supported by efficient working capital management and optimisation of capital expenditure.
Pursue steady margin expansion through a disciplined approach to unit economics, leveraging increasing scale and integrating AI into operations to drive operating efficiencies.

Continue to expand the physical retail store footprint while making deliberate investments to acquire new customers, improve order-to-delivery speeds and leverage technology and automation for efficiency.

The Company commits to granular, comprehensive segment-level disclosure for its two core segments - Beauty and Fashion - through quarterly results, quarterly revenue updates and annual disclosures, alongside quarterly earnings calls and an annual Investor Day.

Superstore (eB2B) reached ~Rs 1,200 cr GMV in 4 years with ~0.5M retailers across 1,300 cities and +500bps EBITDA improvement; ~30% of orders now self-serve, continuing scale-led unit economics gains (steady-state single-digit margin business).

Beauty vertical EBITDA at 9.6% FY26 (10.3% Q4, +70bps YoY); each sub-business independently improving margins, but core beauty retail will reinvest efficiency gains into growth, so similar year-over-year margin trajectory can be expected all else equal.
Continue investing in core growth engines while taking a phased approach to investing in new, emerging opportunity areas through organic initiatives or strategic inorganic acquisitions.
Nykaa Fashion has managed Nike's India digital commerce (Nike.com + Nike app) end-to-end since February; early signs positive in the first few months of this differentiated (non-marketplace) model.
India-UK and India-EU free trade agreements could lower import duties on beauty/cosmetics, a potential net positive improving brand access and pricing, but not yet quantified and pending detail.
Signed partnerships with YouTube (integrating shopping into videos) and Snapchat (nurturing next-gen Gen Z beauty creators), leveraging Nykaa's 100,000+ influencer affiliate network.
Board approved acquiring the remaining 40% stake in nutricosmetics brand Nudge for Rs 14.2 lakh, taking Nykaa to 100% to sharpen focus on health and wellness.
Board approved acquiring an additional 39% stake in Dot & Key (taking Nykaa to 90%) for Rs 265 cr; brand at ~Rs 750 cr annualized GMV run rate and profitable since Q4CY23.
Board approved infusing Rs 150 cr additional equity into Nykaa Fashion (conversion of parent loan into equity) to capitalize the business and lower its interest cost.
Superstore (eB2B) to add a few more warehouses (aim of at least one per state) on top of the existing 13, superimposed on the e-commerce warehouse network.

verdicts.item: Physical retail at 187 stores across 68 cities (GMV +50% 3yr, EBITDA +105%); rolling out larger, more impactful flagship stores (first at Linking Road) with more to come in coming months and years.
verdicts.note: 'we have more than doubled our retail footprint over the past 3 years' with multiple new experiential/flagship formats - continued rollout of larger/differentiated stores.

verdicts.item: Owned brand Dot & Key hit ~Rs 580 cr+ annualized GMV in Q4FY24 and, on March momentum, is likely to annualize to Rs 700 cr+; profitable since Jan-2023 with offline distribution being added.
verdicts.note: 'This brand grew enormously in the last 3 years at 13x, delivering INR 1,790 crores of GMV' - far exceeding the Rs 700 cr+ expectation. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Capex is significantly lower in FY24 vs FY23 as office and warehouse investment is largely complete; company will continue to invest in retail expansion and tech capabilities.
verdicts.note: 'Our capex utilization... currently stands at about 1% of revenue... We continue to invest in beauty retail store expansion, fulfilment capabilities as well as technology' - low-capex, retail/tech-inv…

verdicts.item: By September 2024, ~70-80% of orders from the top 12 metros and ~50% of orders from the next ~110 cities to be fulfilled same-day/next-day, taking ~50% of all India orders to same/next-day delivery.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 6Q past horizon Q2FY25

verdicts.item: The elevated-discounting cycle that widened the GMV vs Net Revenue gap is at its end; from here GMV and Net Revenue growth are expected to be similar.
verdicts.note: Record gross margin and net-revenue growth confirm the discounting cycle ended and GMV/NSV growth converged.

verdicts.item: Board approved acquiring a majority stake in D2C clean-beauty brand Earth Rhythm (making it a subsidiary); Q1FY25 GMV ~Rs 55 cr, grown 8x over 3 years off a small base.
verdicts.note: 'We had acquired 76% stake in Earth Rhythm... and we now completed the acquisition by acquiring an additional 24% stake' - majority stake taken and fully completed.

verdicts.item: Prestige fragrance market share reached ~13% in FY24 (+300bps YoY) and is expected to keep improving in FY25 as fragrance becomes the third core beauty pillar.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Superstore (eB2B) grew 72% YoY with contribution margin +520bps and is on its journey toward breakeven per the long-term plan.
verdicts.note: 'because of our growing scale... we have improved our EBITDA margin by greater than 500 bps' - breakeven journey continuing but not yet reached.

verdicts.item: Within the Beauty vertical, the most meaningful margin improvement is expected to come from the eB2B (Superstore) business scaling, while beauty.com/retail margins stay healthy and owned brands grow faster than the platform.
verdicts.note: 'each business is independently seeing improvement in their margin profile' with eB2B improving and owned brands outpacing - Beauty-vertical margin-mix improvement as described.

verdicts.item: Services (ad) income and demand expected to strengthen in H2FY25 (festive season) as D2C brands return to advertising and discounting moderates on demand revival, aiding BPC gross margins.
verdicts.note: 'gross margin improving by 132 basis points in FY '26, led by strong performance of House of Nykaa and improved service income across businesses' - services/ad income strengthened as expected.

verdicts.item: Management retains Investor Day guidance to break even in the Fashion vertical at EBITDA level during FY26; Q1 EBITDA improved to -6.2% (+304bps YoY).
verdicts.note: 'we reported a positive 30 basis points EBITDA for the fourth quarter' and 'Fashion has become profitable' - FY26 breakeven guidance delivered.

verdicts.item: Fashion grew 25% GMV, above market, and management believes it will sustainably and comfortably outstrip market growth in the coming quarters as a structural improvement.
verdicts.note: 'the financial year '26 was 30% growth, almost reaching INR 5,000 crores in GMV' with an accelerating exit - sustained above-market growth as claimed.

wtt.summary: 75% guidance hit (14 chains); 5/6 projects on-time; 2 expired; 18% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: Highly confident, framing FY26 as a record year of profitable growth with 14 quarters of sustained mid-20s growth; management stayed disciplined on not giving hard forward numbers, flagged macro/currency/inflation caution, and repeatedly stressed reinvesting margin gains back into growth.

meta.thesis: Nykaa delivered record revenue and profitability growth in FY26, with EBITDA margin expanding to 7.5% and PAT margin hitting 2%, driven by accelerated growth in House of Nykaa brands and profitable turnaround in Fashion; the company is now a dominant omnichannel platform in beauty and fashion with AI-enhanced customer acquisition and brand partnerships like Nike and H&M creating new revenue streams.
